Exercise A

A Country Made for Sport

Read the text and fill in each gap with the correct word.

Before you read — optional, not marked
This is just to get you thinking — you can leave it empty and it does not count towards your score.
Reading text

Canada is a country made for sport, in every season. In winter, millions of Canadians play ice hockey — on frozen lakes, on streets and in huge indoor arenas. For many families, hockey is more than a game: it is part of who they are. Lacrosse, a fast and physical team sport, is the official summer sport. First Nations 1 it for hundreds of years before Europeans arrived in North America. Even basketball has Canadian roots: James Naismith, who 2 the game in 1891, was born in Ontario.

Right now, as autumn turns to winter, Canadian communities are preparing for the cold months. City workers are flooding outdoor ice rinks, and children are waiting for the first frost to play outside again. Every weekend, families head to the 3 to ski or snowboard. In Ottawa, some people even skate to work on the frozen 4 Canal.

When they are not playing sport, Canadians spend their free time outdoors. In summer they hike, camp and 5 in the wilderness. In autumn, many simply watch the forests turn 6 and gold. Sport and nature go together in Canada — and visitors are always 7 to join in. So if you ever go, pack your skates and your sense of adventure — you will 8 both of them.

Exercise B

Present Simple or Present Continuous?

Choose the correct form. The present simple is for habits and facts; the present continuous is for things happening now.

On and off the ice

1. Every winter, millions of Canadians ice hockey.

2. Look! The children on the frozen lake right now.

3. Lacrosse from an Indigenous game with hundreds of years of history.

4. Right now, the city workers the outdoor rink.

5. Water at 0°C — that is simple physics.

6. My Canadian exchange partner for a ski marathon at the moment.

7. Every Saturday night, hockey fans across Canada the NHL on television.

8. Shh! The final right now.

3. I what you mean; the winters there are freezing.

Exercise D

Writing: Dear Jordan …

Your Canadian exchange partner is coming to your school for a week in June. Write an email (6–8 sentences) telling them what sports your class usually does and what you are planning for their visit. Use at least three present simple and two present continuous forms.

Useful phrases
You can use these: In our sports lessons we usually … At the moment we are … Right now I am … Every Friday we … We are planning to …
Your email
Aim for 6–8 sentences: 3+ present simple, 2+ present continuous.
